log.text: Liftoff. The Moon in the window: 20° left. Fuel for 48 s of burn.
Target centred in the window (+4°). DNp20: right 35 Hz, left 35 Hz.
Out of the dense air: altitude 36, speed 17 u/s.
The Moon is blinding. The retina turns its sensitivity down to 50%.
Target held centred for 10.0 s without a break.
Flight computer: flip, engines first. Altitude 163, closing 39 u/s. The pilot's lever is off for the manoeuvre.
Meteor M-4 in the window (38° right, 11% of the Moon's light). The pilot held its course.
Meteor M-1 in the window (41° right, 13% of the Moon's light). The pilot held its course.
Flip complete, landing burn. The pilot now looks through the landing camera; its lever moves the rocket sideways.
The pad never came to the centre of the camera: closest 6° left.
Flight computer: altitude 20. Below this the sideways speed is limited in proportion to height; the direction stays the pilot's.
Touchdown: 1.5 u/s down, 0.4 u/s sideways, ground slope 14°, 5.3 u from the centre of the pad.

The legs' signal reached 2,522 leg mechanosensory neurons. In 0.5 s the ascending neurons (legs → brain) fired 15,941 spikes, against 0 before contact. Strongest in the brain: PEN_a(PEN1) (+1,831), PEN_b(PEN2) (+1,722), cells with no named type (+1,566).

cause: CAUSE: the rocket tipped over after touchdown — ground slope 14°, above the 12° the legs can stand on. The pad was 5 u away.
